question_text: Mara passed the Civil Service Exam and is now applying for a government position. She wants to know which type of eligibility she needs for a supervisory role that involves policy formulation. Which of the following correctly describes the difference between Sub-Professional and Professional eligibility?

options.text: Sub-Professional eligibility qualifies one for all first-level positions, while Professional eligibility is required for second-level positions involving supervision and policy-making.
Both eligibilities allow appointment to any position in the government, regardless of level.
Professional eligibility is only for positions in the national government, while Sub-Professional is for local government units.
Sub-Professional eligibility is for positions requiring a bachelor's degree, while Professional eligibility is for those with a master's degree.
